name: Mirror
desc: A hall where everyone looks at others

text.y: This is the Hall of Mirrors. Here the children look not at themselves, but at others. Help them.
text.t: This is the Hall of Mirrors. The children who live here look not at themselves, but at others. Every mirror shows someone “better.” Help them.

steps.text: “Ari plays football better than me. Why should I even go out on the pitch?”

options.t: Copy every one of Ari's tricks
options.r: Dani learned a couple of Ari's tricks, and one really came in handy. But playing entirely “like Ari” didn't work: it's someone else's style. After a week Dani was worn out.

options.t: Get upset and give up football
options.r: For the first few days Dani even felt better: nobody to compare himself with. And then he started missing the ball. Maybe it was just a break?

options.t: Notice what he has himself
options.r: Dani realised: he sees the field better than anyone and makes precise passes. The coach put him in the centre, and Ari scored from his pass.

options.t: Prove that he is better
options.r: Dani started training twice as much and really did improve. Only now he never passes to anyone, and the team finds it harder to play with him.

options.t: Talk to the coach
options.r: The coach said: “I don't need two Aris. I need Dani.” And he gave him a list of exercises. It turned out to be a lot of work, and the first weeks were not easy.

steps.text: “Shira is smarter than me. For her all the problems just solve themselves.”

options.t: Study late into the night, exactly like Shira
options.r: Mira's marks went up a little. But she doesn't get enough sleep, and she is bored. It seems she has a different way of learning.

options.t: Decide that she is stupid and stop trying
options.r: Mira felt calmer: she doesn't have to compete with anyone. But nobody ever heard her excellent questions.

options.t: Find what she herself is strong at
options.r: Mira noticed: she explains things better than anyone. When she retells a topic, the whole class understands. Even Shira asks her for help with history.

options.t: Look for Shira's mistakes and laugh at them
options.r: Mira found a mistake and laughed. For a minute it felt nice, then awkward for both of them. And her own problems didn't get solved that way.

options.t: Ask Shira how she studies
options.r: Shira shared her methods. Half of them didn't suit Mira. But she took one and understood: you can learn in your own way.

steps.text: “Eli has loads of friends, and I have only two.”

options.t: Act like Eli: joke louder than everyone
options.r: People really did laugh at a couple of jokes, and that felt good. But Levi feels he is playing a part. That wears you out quickly.

options.t: Sit alone: nothing will work out anyway
options.r: Being alone is sometimes useful. But his friends have invited Levi three times already, and he didn't go. Now they invite him less often.

options.t: Remember what kind of friend he is
options.r: Levi realised: he has few friends, but very close ones. He knows how to keep secrets and comes when things are bad. Many people look for a friend like that.

options.t: Tell everyone that Eli is a show-off
options.r: Someone agreed with him, and for a minute Levi was the centre of attention. Then the rumour reached Eli. And Levi did not become any closer to his friends.

options.t: Invite his two friends to do something new
options.r: The three of them went on a hike. It was cold and there were mosquitoes, but they talked by the campfire half the night. It turned out friendship isn't about numbers.

steps.text: “Tali draws like a real artist. And nothing I do comes out right.”

options.t: Draw the same pictures as Tali
options.r: By copying, Chana learned a lot: her lines became more confident. But at the exhibition you can't tell whose work is whose. Chana herself isn't there yet.

options.t: Throw away her paints
options.r: The paints are in the bin. At first she felt relieved. But in the evening Chana remembered how she loved making up stories for her drawings.

options.t: Notice that she has something of her own
options.r: Chana realised: her strength is making up stories. Together with Tali she made a comic: Tali draws, Chana writes. The whole school reads it.

options.t: Say that drawing is nonsense
options.r: Someone agreed with Chana. But it didn't feel any better: inside it still hurts.

options.t: Ask Tali what she likes about Chana
options.r: Tali was surprised: “But you're the best at coming up with plots!” Chana had never even thought about it.

steps.text: What did you notice in the Hall of Mirrors?

options.t: Comparing takes away your strength
options.r: Yes. While you look into someone else's mirror, your own work stands still.

options.t: Everyone found something of their own
options.r: Yes. And it was found only when the hero stopped looking at someone else.

options.t: Someone else's success takes nothing away from you
options.r: Yes. Ari scored the goal, but it was Dani who gave the pass.

options.t: It's not all so simple
options.r: Exactly. Almost every choice had both pluses and minuses. That's how it is in life too.

steps.text: Someone else's strength does not make yours weaker.
steps.sub: The mirrors go dark. One after another they begin to show the children themselves.
